mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting glucagon to the liver was most worthwhile because the result showed stored glycogen supplying blood glucose and the signal diminishing afterward.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining the meal glucose with the body first was a slightly confusing prerequisite; I initially expected the sensing cells to respond directly to the blood.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the blood first had to be connected to the body before the pancreatic cells could sense it.

arbitrary.text: That initial body-connection requirement felt somewhat arbitrary because the glucose-rich blood and sensing cells already seemed like a plausible pair.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue: seeing the insulin and glucagon responses linked to changes in blood glucose made me curious about how other body systems regulate themselves.
